entries.content_plain:
CHAPTER 4
 
Jos 4:1-8. Twelve Stones Taken for a Memorial Out of Jordan.

1-3. the Lord spake unto Joshua, Take you twelve men--each representing a tribe. They had been previously chosen for this service (Jos 3:12), and the repetition of the command is made here solely to introduce the account of its execution. Though Joshua had been divinely instructed to erect a commemorative pile, the representatives were not apprised of the work they were to do till the time of the passage.

Joshua called the twelve men--</hi>They had probably, from a feeling of reverence, kept back, and were standing on the eastern bank. They were now ordered to advance. entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1995"/><div sID="gen2657" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1995"/><hi type="bold">6-7. That this may be a sign among you--</hi>The erection of cairns, or huge piles of stones, as monuments of remarkable incidents has been common among all people, especially in the early and rude periods of their history. They are the established means of perpetuating the memory of important transactions, especially among the nomadic people of the East. Although there be no inscription engraved on them, the history and object of such simple monuments are traditionally preserved from age to age. Similar was the purpose contemplated by the conveyance of the twelve stones to Gilgal: it was that they might be a standing record to posterity of the miraculous passage of the Jordan. <div eID="gen2657" type="x-p"/>

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1997"/><title type="x-s3"><reference osisRef="Josh.4.9">Jos 4:9</reference>. Twelve Stones Set Up in the Midst of Jordan.</title> <div sID="gen2659" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1997"/><hi type="bold">9. Joshua set up twelve stones ... in the place where the feet of the priests ... stood--</hi>In addition to the memorial just described, there was another memento of the miraculous event, a duplicate of the former, set up in the river itself, on the very spot where the ark had rested. This heap of stones might have been a large and compactly built one and visible in the ordinary state of the river. As nothing is said where these stones were obtained, some have imagined that they might have been gathered in the adjoining fields and deposited by the people as they passed the appointed spot.<div eID="gen2659" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen2660" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">they are there unto this day--</hi>at least twenty years after the event, if we reckon by the date of this history (<reference osisRef="Josh.24.26">Jos 24:26</reference>), and much later, if the words in the latter clause were inserted by Samuel or Ezra. <div eID="gen2660" type="x-p"/>
entries.content_plain:
Jos 4:9. Twelve Stones Set Up in the Midst of Jordan.

9. Joshua set up twelve stones ... in the place where the feet of the priests ... stood--In addition to the memorial just described, there was another memento of the miraculous event, a duplicate of the former, set up in the river itself, on the very spot where the ark had rested. This heap of stones might have been a large and compactly built one and visible in the ordinary state of the river. As nothing is said where these stones were obtained, some have imagined that they might have been gathered in the adjoining fields and deposited by the people as they passed the appointed spot.
 
they are there unto this day--at least twenty years after the event, if we reckon by the date of this history (Jos 24:26), and much later, if the words in the latter clause were inserted by Samuel or Ezra.

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1998"/><title type="x-s3"><reference osisRef="Josh.4.10-Josh.4.13">Jos 4:10-13</reference>. The People Pass Over.</title> <div sID="gen2661" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1998"/><hi type="bold">10. the priests which bare the ark stood in the midst of Jordan--</hi>This position was well calculated to animate the people, who probably crossed below the ark, as well as to facilitate Joshua's execution of the minutest instructions respecting the passage (<reference osisRef="Num.27.21-Num.27.23">Nu 27:21-23</reference>). The unfaltering confidence of the priests contrasts strikingly with the conduct of the people, who "hasted and passed over." Their faith, like that of many of God's people, was, through the weakness of nature, blended with fears. But perhaps their "haste" may be viewed in a more favorable light, as indicating the alacrity of their obedience, or it might have been enjoined in order that the the whole multitude might pass in one day. <div eID="gen2661" type="x-p"/>
entries.content_plain:
Jos 4:10-13. The People Pass Over.

10. the priests which bare the ark stood in the midst of Jordan--This position was well calculated to animate the people, who probably crossed below the ark, as well as to facilitate Joshua's execution of the minutest instructions respecting the passage (Nu 27:21-23). entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1999"/><div sID="gen2662" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1999"/><hi type="bold">11. the ark of the Lord passed over, and the priests, in the presence of the people--</hi>The ark is mentioned as the efficient cause; it had been the first to move--it was the last to leave--and its movements arrested the deep attention of the people, who probably stood on the opposite bank, wrapt in admiration and awe of this closing scene.
